page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7se.large is an entry-level compute-optimized instance type powered by the KVM hypervisor. The instance is built on an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.9 GHz, providing 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with 2 threads. Hardware specifications include 4.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU), a 48 MB L3 cache, and support for hardware instruction extensions such as AVX-512 VNNI, AES, and SHA_NI. The instance includes no local storage and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance data reveals a strong contrast between single-threaded and multi-threaded throughput. Single-core tests show average relative performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1559.0, a stress-ng single-core result of 1858.29, and single-threaded gzip compression at 27.69 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks rank in the lower percentiles due to the single physical core layout, yielding a PassMark CPU score of 2990.49 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 1813.0. Potentially uncached memory bandwidth is also limited, recording 14.89 GB/sec for large block reads and 13.52 GB/sec for large block writes.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and low multi-threading density, the ecs.c7se.large offers a specialized profile for light, non-parallelized execution requirements. Tested throughput includes 3.56 GB/sec for static web serving and 1.97 million operations per second in Redis SET tasks. The hardware profile is best suited for entry-level microservices, basic text processing, single-threaded scripts, and lightweight background utility tasks that require dedicated CPU execution without high memory or multi-core demands.

Benchmark data indicates solid single-core CPU execution, achieving average ratings in single-threaded tests such as Geekbench single-core (1559.0). However, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth test results rank in the lower percentiles due to core count limitations. With its 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation, the ecs.c7se.large offers basic compute capabilities tailored for low-concurrency workloads, simple text processing tasks, lightweight web serving, and small background processes requiring predictable single-threaded CPU performance.
